Ørsted narrows its quarterly loss to €96 million despite US impairments
sum: Ørsted narrowed its third-quarter net loss to 726 million Danish kroner (€96 million), compared with 1.7 billion kroner in the same period of 2025. The Danish group, which specializes in offshore wind development, remains weighed down by its activities in the United States. It booked 3.4 billion kroner of impairments there, or €449 million. These figures cover the period from July to September.

US impairments continue to weigh on the quarter's result. Ørsted's American projects, a historic leader in offshore wind, have been slowed by opposition from Donald Trump. The group recorded 3.4 billion Danish kroner (€449 million) on this account.

Despite this charge, the net loss fell compared with the third quarter of the previous year, from 1.7 billion kroner to 726 million. Revenue for the quarter reached 21 billion Danish kroner, up 73% year on year. Ørsted attributes this increase to higher output, driven by stronger wind speeds and higher electricity prices.

Output from offshore wind farms rose 19% over the quarter, to 4.5 TWh (terawatt-hours). According to the group, this reflects more favorable wind conditions. Higher electricity prices also supported revenue, Ørsted says.

Output from onshore turbines increased 4%, to 3.4 TWh. The increase is therefore less pronounced than for offshore wind. In the information available, Ørsted did not detail the respective contributions of wind and prices to the rise in revenue.

At 08:15 GMT, shortly after the opening of the Copenhagen stock exchange, Ørsted shares were up 2.11%. The market was stable at the time. Investors had the third-quarter figures in hand, marked by a narrower loss and by US impairments of €449 million.

How Election Backing For Clean Energy Has Changed Ørsted Stock Investment Story
sum: Ørsted, a major Danish renewable energy group with a significant share of the global offshore wind market, recently saw its sector lifted as solar and wind stocks reacted positively to election results that supported expectations for faster clean energy development.

The market reaction highlights how sensitive Ørsted’s economics are to policy sentiment, since project returns depend heavily on regulation, power pricing frameworks, and hedging conditions across its offshore and onshore portfolio.
We now consider how this renewed, policy-driven optimism around offshore wind could shape Ørsted’s broader investment narrative.

Scan policy sensitive clean energy opportunities moving with Ørsted’s momentum by reviewing the hand picked 41 power grid technology and infrastructure stocks that could benefit from similar market tailwinds.

Owning Ørsted means believing in a capital heavy build out of offshore and onshore renewables where disciplined project selection and execution really matter. The group controls a sizeable slice of global offshore wind, yet still reports a loss of DKK 3,118m on DKK 83,672m of revenue. Policy friendly election results that lifted clean energy stocks support sentiment around future project pipelines, but they do not resolve the basic reality that returns hinge on power price frameworks, hedging, and contract terms for a long list of projects already committed.

In the short term, the key swing factors remain operational rather than political. Ørsted needs to translate elevated electricity pricing into sustainable cash flow while funding large projects without stretching a balance sheet backed entirely by higher risk borrowing, not customer deposits. Forecasts that earnings could grow and turn profitable over the next three years support the story, and recent share gains alongside a discount to some valuation estimates show how quickly confidence can move. Ørsted to take full control of UK’s Gunfleet Sands offshore wind farm
sum: Ørsted will take full ownership of the Gunfleet Sands 1 & 2 Offshore Wind Farm off the Essex coast by acquiring the remaining 49.9% stake from investment partners for about GBP 15 million. The 172 MW project, operational since 2010 and generating enough renewable electricity to power over 125,000 UK homes annually, will be wholly owned and operated by Ørsted once the deal closes, expected in November subject to customary conditions.

The move allows Ørsted to capture the full value of the asset and gain greater flexibility in managing Gunfleet Sands, including assessing potential lifetime extension and other late-life options. By exercising a long-standing buyback right, Ørsted is reinforcing its strategy of maximising the performance and long-term value of its operating assets in the UK offshore wind market, where its 12 operational wind farms already supply roughly 7% of national electricity demand.

Ørsted A/S is a Denmark-headquartered renewable energy group and a global leader in developing, constructing and operating offshore wind farms, with a core focus on European markets. The company has 11 GW of installed offshore capacity and 7.2 GW under construction, contributing to more than 19 GW of total renewable capacity across Europe, Asia Pacific and North America, including onshore wind, solar, energy storage, bioenergy plants and energy trading.

Widely recognised for its sustainability credentials, Ørsted aims to enable a world fully powered by green energy and operates an extensive offshore wind fleet in the UK that supplies about 7% of the country’s electricity. The group, listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen, employs around 7,300 people and reported operating profit of DKK 25.1 billion in 2025, underlining its scale in the global clean energy sector.

Ørsted (CPSE:ORSTED) Starts Blackwater Solar, Is The Stock Undervalued?
sum: Blackwater Solar construction puts Ørsted stock back in focus

Ørsted (CPSE:ORSTED) has started construction on Blackwater Solar, a 200 MW project in Roosevelt County, New Mexico. It is the company's first development in the state and is part of its US onshore build out.

Investors have taken notice of Ørsted again, with a 1-day share price return of 3.30% and a year-to-date share price gain of 8.95%. This short-term momentum comes against a backdrop of a 5-year total shareholder return that is down 68.78%.
Scan 40 power grid technology and infrastructure stocks for other renewables and grid-focused plays investors are watching as Ørsted expands its US solar presence with Blackwater Solar.

The bounce in Ørsted after the Blackwater Solar update raises a simple tension. Do the current setbacks and valuation gap still skew the balance toward buyers, or has the easy part of the rerating already passed?

Ørsted closed at DKK139.45, while Simply Wall St's DCF model currently estimates future cash flow value at DKK335.62, which implies the shares are trading at a steep discount. On top of that, the stock carries a P/S ratio of 2.2x, and that becomes more interesting when set against both peers and the wider renewable energy space.

The P/S multiple looks at what investors are paying for each unit of revenue that Ørsted generates. For a utility scale renewables operator with sizeable offshore and onshore assets, revenue is a key reference point because earnings are currently negative and can be heavily affected by impairments, build out cycles and power price swings.

Prince William and Princess Kate celebrate finalist in future king's beloved Earthshot Prize
sum: Prince William and Princess Kate have celebrated one of the finalists in the Earthshot Prize on Instagram – as Prince Harry appeared at the WellChild Awards in London.

The Prince and Princess of Wales shared a post about Ørsted, the Danish energy company which has transformed itself from one of Europe's most coal-intensive utilities into the world's largest offshore wind operator.
The company is among the 15 finalists for the 2026 Earthshot Prize, which was founded by the future king to find and support solutions to some of the world's biggest environmental challenges.
Ørsted has been shortlisted in the Fix Our Climate category after cutting its own Scope 1 and 2 emissions by more than 98 per cent and shifting away from coal, oil and gas towards renewable energy.
The Prince and Princess of Wales' official Instagram account highlighted the company's transformation, drawing attention to its role in the global shift towards clean energy.
The Earthshot Prize describes Ørsted as having transformed from one of Europe's most coal-intensive utilities into a global leader in offshore wind.
The post comes as Prince Harry makes a high-profile appearance of his own in London.

Offshore drilling deal between Energy Holdings and Venture Offshore
sum: Energy Holdings and Ventura Offshore have signed a letter of intent for an all-share combination.
The combination creates a larger and more diversified listed energy services platform with approximately USD 1.3 billion in contracted revenue backlog.

Under the proposed transaction, Energy Holdings will acquire 100% of Ventura Offshore. Existing Energy Holdings shareholders are expected to own approximately 55% of the combined company, with Ventura Offshore shareholders holding approximately 45%.
Based on Energy Holdings’ closing share price on 10 September 2026, the combined group would have an implied pro forma equity value of approximately USD 1 billion.

The transaction is expected to strengthen cash generation, financial flexibility and the capacity for shareholder distributions, while creating additional growth opportunities in offshore drilling and related services.
Completion is targeted for Q1 2027, subject to definitive agreements, due diligence and customary shareholder, court and regulatory approvals.
Following completion, Energy Holdings will remain the listed parent company, and management also intends to evaluate a potential US dual listing and IPO.
